Extensions: When iid Assumptions Change

Three extra-credit investigations and one creative application

Four investigations

  • Dependent machine failures use a conditional Exponential rate determined by the previous operating time.
  • Non-identical Bernoulli observations preserve independence while probabilities decline from 0.90 to 0.50.
  • Synthetic age-at-death mixture applies the ordinary iid CLT to a bounded two-component construction.
  • Heritage-language creative case compares neutral equal-mean probability paths and adds one accessible interactive thought experiment.

Results at a glance

shown <- decisions[, c("case_id", "ordinary_iid_clt", "generalized_or_iid_framework", "smallest_defensible_n", "conclusion", "key_caveat")]

shown$smallest_defensible_n[is.na(shown$smallest_defensible_n)] <- "None through 2000"

knitr::kable(shown, row.names = FALSE)

Central lesson

The phrase “the CLT works” is incomplete unless the theorem and process are named. The synthetic age mixture fits the ordinary iid framework. The changing Bernoulli and creative paths need a bounded independent-array argument. The machine-failure process is dependent and receives empirical, simulation-referenced comparisons rather than an invented iid SE.

Reproducibility

All authoritative static results use seed 631 and 10,000 repetitions. The dependent case receives a seed-1631 and burn-in sensitivity check. Only compact summaries are committed. The creative browser tool is supplemental, deterministic, local, and paired with a complete static fallback.
